audit.why: 47.60% over 208 games — a losing lane on a modest but usable sample.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 is marked Skill where whys[0] says 'concede the opening'; level 3 is Kled where whys[2] says 'genuinely even'; levels 4-5 are Skill where whys[3] calls them 'your weakest window'; level 6 is Skill where whys[4] calls it 'your one clean window to flip the lane'; and first item is Kled where whys[5] says 'a coinflip'.
audit.why: Kled bullies the early skirmish levels and out-scales late; Ambessa's single owned stage is level 6, where a 1250-unit suppress catches a champion whose escape is a recastable dash.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Kled / Kled / Skill / Kled / Ambessa / Skill / Kled in both layers — Kled 4, Skill 2, Ambessa 1, which fits 47.60% and matches every why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Kled's ultimate is misnamed in three places as 'Chaaaaaarge!! (R)'. Riot's name is Chaaaaaaaarge!!! — seven a's and three exclamation marks. Its cooldown, range and shield are all absent, and Ambessa's level 6 is credited twice to an 'armor-pen burst' that appears in Riot's text for none of her abilities.
audit.why: Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is 140/125/110 seconds at 3500/4000/4500 range, and it grants a shield on the way in. Two things follow: it is a map-wide engage rather than a lane tool, so 'his R re-opens every fight' understates it badly; and the shield means committing your burst into a fresh charge wastes it, which is exactly the interaction the derived data flags. It is also LONGER than Ambessa's 130-second ultimate at rank 1, so the level 6 trade of ultimates favours her.
audit.corrected: Name spelled correctly in three fields, with 140s, the 3500-4500 range and the shield stated in late, whys[6], spikes[3].text, wants.foe[2] and phases[4].why. Penetration claims removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two of Kled's abilities are absent from the page and the third has its counterplay missing. Jousting (E) — a 550-range dash that can be RECAST to dash back through the initial target — is never mentioned once, despite being his mobility, his engage and his disengage. Violent Tendencies (W) is only ever called 'mounted aggression'. And Bear Trap on a Rope is described as 'if he ropes you he reels you in', when Riot's text says the yank only happens 'if shackled for a short duration'.
audit.why: All three change what you do. The yank is conditional, so a Drakehound's Step out of range during the shackle window cancels the pull entirely — that turns his engage from unavoidable into dodgeable. Violent Tendencies is four fast attacks with the fourth dealing extra damage, so the burst is a countable window with a visible tell rather than ambient pressure. And Jousting's recast means gluing him with Lacerate has a specific purpose: it is the return dash you are trying to deny, not just chase prevention.
audit.corrected: Jousting named in whys[2], mid, phases[2].why and report[5].t. Violent Tendencies named with the four-attack tell in early, whys[1], wants.foe[0] and breakdown.cooldowns. The conditional yank stated in early, spikes[0].text, wants.foe[0], report[5].t and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Kled's remount as passive sustain — 'his remount keeps Skaarl topped up', 'his remount out-sustains your energy refunds'.
audit.why: Riot's passive: 'Kled can restore Skaarl's courage by fighting enemies. At maximum courage, Kled remounts with a portion of Skaarl's health.' The remount is not a regeneration timer, it is paid for by fighting you. That inverts the advice: against a dismounted Kled the mistake is a long trade, because your own trade is the resource he is spending to get back on. Dismounted he also deals less damage to champions, so the correct play is a short decisive burst or nothing.
audit.corrected: Stated in mid, whys[3], whys[5], spikes[2].text, wants.foe[1] and dontsFull[1], with the reduced dismounted damage added as the reason to pick that window.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Use it the moment his Bear Trap on a Rope (Q) is down' names no cooldown, and neither does anything else on the page.
audit.why: Bear Trap on a Rope is 11/10/9/8/7s at 800 range; Violent Tendencies and Jousting are both 13/12/11/10/9s. Those three roughly matching timers are why his pressure feels continuous — there is no long gap to wait out, which is precisely why the level 6 suppress matters more here than a cooldown-counting plan would.
audit.corrected: Real numbers added to whys[1], spikes[0].text and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer spells the ability 'Beartrap on a Rope' as one word throughout, while the content layer spells it correctly as 'Bear Trap on a Rope'.
audit.why: Riot's name is Bear Trap on a Rope. The two layers of the same matchup printing different spellings is the kind of inconsistency that makes a page look machine-generated.
audit.corrected: Corrected in the writable full-layer fields I touched: dosFull[0].t, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns and phases[2].why.

edits.before: Kled owns the opening. He's a level 1-3 skirmish bully and you're at your weakest — one ability, no combo, energy-gated, with very long early cooldowns. Do not step into Bear Trap on a Rope (Q) range; if he ropes you he reels you in and dumps full mounted aggression you can't trade back through. Last-hit with the outer edge of Cunning Sweep (Q) from max range and accept the chip. Bait nothing here — your dash-weave trades don't beat his mounted pressure yet, so just farm toward six.
edits.after: Kled owns the opening. He's a level 1-3 skirmish bully and you're at your weakest — one ability, no combo, energy-gated, with very long early cooldowns. Bear Trap on a Rope (Q) reaches 800 and only yanks you in if the shackle holds for a moment, so a Drakehound's Step out of range cancels the pull. Otherwise last-hit with the outer edge of Cunning Sweep from max range and accept the chip. Violent Tendencies (W) is his tell: four fast attacks, and the fourth hits hardest.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still his — your cooldowns are longest here and his remount keeps Skaarl topped up, so keep farming and don't force. Level 6 is your flip: Public Execution (R) blinks you behind Kled, suppresses through his mounted aggression, and crashes him down with armor-pen burst. Use it the moment his Bear Trap on a Rope (Q) is down, ideally while he's dismounted — that's your cleanest kill of the lane. Land Lacerate (E) to slow and glue him so he can't kite the followup, and brace Repudiation (W) into his remount aggression to amp your next slam.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still his — your cooldowns are longest here and he restores Skaarl's courage by fighting you, so every long trade is paying for his remount. Level 6 is your flip: Public Execution (R) blinks 1250 units, suppresses and crashes him down. Use it the moment Bear Trap on a Rope is down and while he's dismounted, where he deals reduced damage to champions — that's your cleanest kill of the lane. Land Lacerate (E) to glue him so Jousting can't recast back out, and brace Repudiation into the fourth Violent Tendencies hit.

edits.before: This lane drifts back to Kled. He's a hard scaler — HP stacking, remount sustain and a Chaaaaaarge!! (R) engage that re-opens every fight, while your damage stays entirely physical. Once he's got items and an armor component your Q-auto-Q chunks stop landing clean and his remount out-sustains your energy refunds. Win it on your Level 6 and first-item windows or not at all; if it goes long, group and use Public Execution (R) as a pick tool rather than soloing a fed remount-Kled.
edits.after: This lane drifts back to Kled. He's a hard scaler — HP stacking, remount sustain, and a Chaaaaaaaarge!!! (R) that crosses 3500 to 4500 units and hands him a shield on the way in, so it re-opens every fight and eats the front of your burst. Once he's got an armour component your Q-auto-Q chunks stop landing clean. Win it on your Level 6 and first-item windows or not at all; if it goes long, use Public Execution as a pick tool rather than soloing him.

notes: Kled's ultimate was misspelled as 'Chaaaaaarge!! (R)' in three fields — Riot's name has seven a's and three exclamation marks. Jousting (E) and Violent Tendencies (W) appeared nowhere on the page at all, which means his dash, his disengage and his burst window were all invisible to the reader. The most useful recovery is the conditional on Bear Trap on a Rope: Riot's text says the yank happens 'if shackled for a short duration', so it is dodgeable by a champion with three dashes, and the page had it as an unavoidable reel-in. Second most useful is the remount rule — courage is earned by fighting, so an extended trade against a dismounted Kled is how you put him back on Skaarl. Both derived interactions the data flagged for this matchup checked out against Riot's text and are now on the page: the Chaaaaaaaarge!!! shield and the Violent Tendencies auto-reset tell. Unverified and removed rather than restated: Ambessa's 'armor-pen burst' on Public Execution, which appears in two fields here and across her whole matchup set.
